metadata.title: Server Configuration and Baseline

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for defining, declaring, and assessing secure configuration intent for server execution environments.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Server operating systems, configuration repositories, baseline definitions, and configuration assessment mechanisms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Supporting pattern defining desired‑state configuration intent and drift detection for server platforms.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Treats server configuration as authoritative control data governing execution posture, not as an operational artifact.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Primary control catalog governing secure configuration, least functionality, and baseline management (CM and SI families).

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Guidance on establishing, maintaining, and assessing secure configuration baselines.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Security configuration checklists and benchmark usage for secure system configuration.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Zero Trust guidance establishing that configuration assessment provides signals, not persistent trust.

metadata.remarks: Server Configuration and Baseline defines the authoritative desired state for server configuration and mechanisms to assess drift. This pattern produces configuration posture signals only and does not perform remediation, enforcement, rebuild, or lifecycle actions.

components.title: Server Configuration Baseline Definition
components.description: Defines the approved secure configuration baseline for server environments.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Modification of system configuration to introduce persistence or reduce security controls.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Secure configuration baselines reduce attack surface and unauthorized functionality.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Baseline configurations are formally defined and documented.
Least functionality is enforced through configuration baseline design.

components.title: Server Configuration Assessment
components.description: Assesses server configuration against the approved baseline to identify drift.

props.name: attack-technique
props.remarks: Impairment or disabling of configuration controls to evade detection.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Continuous configuration assessment provides drift detection signals.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Configuration settings are assessed for compliance with approved baselines.
Configuration assessment contributes to continuous monitoring.

components.title: Server Configuration Drift Signaling
components.description: Generates configuration posture and drift signals for downstream trust decisions.

props.name: defense-technique
props.remarks: Explicit signaling prevents configuration drift from being misinterpreted or ignored.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Configuration drift signals inform risk‑based decisions.
